ended: Lost the East Semifinals 3-4 to CLE

archetype.name: Contender That Fell Short (defense-first)
archetype.definition: A 60-win, top-three Net Rtg team built on an elite defense and frontcourt, which survived a seven-game first round and then lost a Game 7 at home in the second round to a division rival it had finished ahead of.

report.headline: A defense-first jump to 60 wins, undone by a Game 7 home blowout

recap.finish: 60-22, first in the Central; beat ORL 4-3, lost the East Semifinals 3-4 to CLE
recap.body:
This was the season Detroit's rebuild turned into a real contender. Two years after a 14-68 finish and one year after a 44-38 breakthrough, the Pistons won 60 games, finished second on the site's Teams tab and posted an 8.2 Net Rtg, third in the league. Nothing about the record was borrowed. W vs Pt Diff sat at exactly 0, and the margin implied the same 60 wins the standings showed. This was a team that beat people, not one that stole close games.

The identity was defense and size. The 109.7 defensive rating ranked second, about six points per 100 possessions better than the league. Detroit led the league in Opp eFG %, Opp 3P % and Opp TOV %, so it took away good shots, contested threes and forced mistakes all at once. That is a rare combination and the clearest sign the defense was structural rather than a hot stretch. Last year's unit ranked 11th, so this was the biggest step forward. The offense was respectable (10th by rating) but unconventional. The Pistons ranked 29th in 3PA Rate, far below the league's share of threes, and made up for it on the glass (third in ORB %) and at the line (fifth in FT Rate).

The frontcourt graded A+, and Jalen Duren was the season's engine. He produced 11 Win Shares on a 68.8 TS %, made the All-Star team and All-NBA Third Team, and Paul Reed (BPM 5.3) kept the level up behind him. Cade Cunningham carried the creation load at a 30.5 USG % and earned All-NBA First Team. Ausar Thompson, All-Defensive First Team, posted a 7.5 On-Off that was the best among the regulars. Below those stars the perimeter was thinner. The backcourt graded B and the wings B-, with Ron Holland (On-Off -5) and Daniss Jenkins (TS 52.5) soaking up big minutes without much return.

The arc was steady excellence with one wobble. A 13-2 November, which included a 13-game winning streak, set the tone. January was the defensive peak, allowing 105.07 points a game. March's 11-7 was the softest month, but the Pistons closed 8-2 over the last ten with their margin above their season mark, so they entered the playoffs playing well.

The playoffs exposed the offense. Against Orlando, Detroit lost Game 1 at home and both games in Orlando before winning the last three, including a 116-94 Game 7. Against Cleveland it won the first two at home, then lost three straight, the last of them in overtime at home. It forced a Game 7 with a 115-94 win on the road, then lost the deciding game at home 94-125. Over the 14 games the team scored 104.93 a game against 117.77 in the regular season. Pace slowed to 94.1, turnovers rose to 14.5 TOV % (14th of 16), and Duren's efficiency fell to a 55.3 TS % with a -9.4 On-Off. The defense mostly held. The half-court offense without spacing did not.

highlights.title: League's best shot-suppression defense
highlights.body: Detroit allowed the lowest Opp eFG % and Opp 3P % in the league and forced the most turnovers by Opp TOV %, for a defensive rating second only to one team. Because it came from every lever at once, and held up in the playoffs (third in Opp eFG % among postseason teams), it looks repeatable rather than lucky.

highlights.title: Duren anchors an A+ frontcourt
highlights.body: Duren's 11 Win Shares on a 68.8 TS % led the roster, and the frontcourt as a group graded A+. With Reed's strong bench minutes behind him, it powered the third-ranked offensive rebounding. This is the core of the team and it is young enough to stay.

highlights.title: A 60-win record fully earned
highlights.body: W vs Pt Diff of 0 means the 60 wins matched the margin exactly. The 8.16 points-per-game differential ranked third. There was no close-game luck to give back, so the baseline next year is a 60-win-caliber team.

lowlights.title: No spacing when games tightened
lowlights.body: Detroit ranked 29th in 3PA Rate, seven points below the league share. That worked in the regular season through offensive rebounds and free throws. In the playoffs scoring fell to 104.93 a game and turnovers rose to 14th of 16 postseason teams. A low-volume three-point offense is easier to load up against in a series, and that is a roster problem, not variance.

lowlights.title: Duren neutralized in the playoffs
lowlights.body: The regular season's most efficient scorer dropped to a 55.3 TS %, a 16.7 USG % and a -9.4 On-Off across 14 playoff games. Cunningham pushed his usage to 32.4 to compensate. A defense that packs the paint takes away the lob-and-putback game when there is little shooting around it.

lowlights.title: Thin perimeter behind the stars
lowlights.body: The wings graded B- and the backcourt B. Holland's -5 On-Off and Jenkins's 52.5 TS % in heavy minutes were the soft spots. Jenkins fell further in the playoffs to a 47.2 TS % and a -11.3 On-Off.

arc.note: A 13-2 November and a 13-game win streak set the pace. Every month was a winning one, with March's 11-7 the only dip, and an 8-2 close carried the team into a playoff run that went the distance twice and ended in a home Game 7 blowout.

recap.nextYear: The foundation carries over. Cunningham, Duren and Thompson earned All-NBA and All-Defensive honors, the frontcourt graded A+, and the 60 wins came with no close-game luck attached. The defense, first in Opp eFG % and Opp TOV %, is the most bankable part of the profile. The work is on the perimeter. The wings (B-) and backcourt depth were the weak groups, and outside of Robinson's 220 threes the team rarely shot from deep. That is what let playoff defenses shrink the floor on Duren and force Cunningham to do everything. Harris (day-to-day) and Stewart (out) end the year injured, worth watching for frontcourt depth. If Detroit adds shooting without giving up its size and defense, the regular-season level should hold. Without it, the playoff ceiling looks a lot like this year's.

confidence.note: Full 82-game season plus 14 playoff games; record matches margin exactly.
